title: Promises: overlap, cancel, and limit work
outcome: Choose sequential or parallel work and prevent stale results without losing useful failures.
benefits: Less avoidable waiting and fewer stale screens.
drawbacks: Parallel requests need per-operation ownership and limits.
version: Modern JavaScript / TypeScript · Vue 3.5 where applicable · browser APIs
cue: Overlap independent work. Bound the amount. Accept only current results.

trace.title: Dependency graph
trace.detail:
## Understand the idea

await describes a dependency: the next line waits for that promise in this function. Two awaits in sequence may waste time when their inputs are independent.

Promise.all waits for all successes but rejects when one rejects; it does not automatically cancel the others. allSettled preserves each outcome when partial results are useful.

Cancellation and acceptance are different. AbortController can stop a supported fetch.

A request number or active flag says whether a result may still update this screen. Guard error and loading state as well as rows.

Parallel does not mean unlimited. Launching 10,000 uploads at once can exhaust memory and connections.

Use a bounded worker pool or a queue. Retry only a safe operation and only within a deliberate attempt/time limit.

trace.title: Follow one item
trace.detail:
Draw the dependency graph. Loading a ticket and a member directory can overlap.

Loading comments using an ID returned by a creation request cannot begin before that ID exists.

For a stale search: A starts, B starts, B succeeds, A fails. The final UI should show B and no stale error.

Use controlled promises to reproduce this exact order. Avoid a fixed sleep as proof.

trace.title: Try the failure
trace.detail: Promise.all does not undo a completed write when another promise fails. A spinner hidden in every finally block can be cleared by obsolete work.
